einzeiler: Federal judge extends block on mail-in voting rules as economic strains hit Americans
kurzfassung: A federal judge has extended an indefinite block on the U.S. Postal Service's efforts to regulate election mail ahead of the midterms. Meanwhile, surging energy costs and inflation are putting immense financial pressure on middle- and lower-income Americans. Additionally, biographer Kai Bird discusses how Roy Cohn's influence and tactics continue to shape Donald Trump's political behavior.
stichpunkte: A Massachusetts federal judge indefinitely extends the block preventing the Postal Service from interfering with mail-in ballots.
Democracy Forward President Skye Perryman emphasizes that citizens must take direct action rather than waiting for a political savior.
August job growth reaches 162,000, but wage growth slows to a five-year low of 3.1%, failing to keep pace with inflation.
U.S. diesel prices hit a record high of $5.85 a gallon, compounding financial strain for middle- and lower-income families.
International allies at the G20 express mounting economic anxiety over U.S. tariff disputes and the ongoing conflict in Iran.
Author Kurt Anderson discusses his new dystopian fiction novel, The Breakup, which imagines an America divided after a national divorce.
Pulitzer Prize-winning biographer Kai Bird explores the lifelong influence of Roy Cohn on Donald Trump's legal and political tactics.

clips.hook: President Trump's renovation plans for Washington
clips.text: Reporters documented the president's obsession with remodeling Washington, including a massive ballroom and a 250-foot arch near Arlington National Cemetery.

clips.hook: Surging diesel prices hit record highs nationwide
clips.text: National diesel prices surged to a record high of $5.85 a gallon, marking an increase of nearly 60 percent compared to the previous year.

clips.hook: Voter disapproval ratings on the economy and living costs
clips.text: Polling data reveals that over half of Americans strongly disapprove of the president's job performance, with 70 percent expressing disapproval regarding his handling of living costs.

clips.hook: Elon Musk's fictional fate in a divided future America
clips.text: In a speculative novel set decades in the future, the nation has dissolved, and billionaire Elon Musk has passed away from an overdose while traveling to Mars.

clips.hook: Roy Cohn's aggressive courtroom tactics against prosecutors
clips.text: During a federal housing discrimination lawsuit, Roy Cohn baselessly accused an assistant prosecutor of blackmailing witnesses to protect his client.

beschreibung:
Tonight on The Last Word: The New York Times reports Iran has grown more confident after six months of war. Also, a federal judge extends the block on Donald Trump’s attack on mail voting. Plus, diesel hits a record high in the U.S. as energy costs surge. Trump ramps up his effort to destroy the Smithsonian. And Trump policies strain economic ties with global allies. Rep. Madeleine Dean, Barbara McQuade, Robert Reich, Skye Perryman, and Heather Long join Jonathan Capehart.
